name: Marlon Duran
bio: Marlon Duran is a community organizer and English-Spanish translator from McAllen, Texas. Born in Mexico, he says he grew up undocumented in the Rio Grande Valley, became a U.S. citizen at 15, and has spent more than a decade organizing with groups including La Union del Pueblo Entero. He is the Green Party of Texas nominee for the 28th Congressional District.

platform.point: Calls for abolishing ICE and for fair, compassionate treatment of undocumented residents in South Texas.
Says living costs keep rising while wages stay low, and argues billionaires and corporations hoard wealth that could support everyone.
Treats climate change as a present problem and faults both major parties and fossil fuel profits for inaction.
Wants to end post-9/11 fear-based security policies and terrorism fearmongering that he says harm border and Muslim communities.
Runs without corporate PAC money and campaigns against the influence of corporate donors and AIPAC.
Backs Palestinian rights and calls for a change in U.S. policy toward Israel and Gaza.
Calls for justice for Indigenous peoples.
Aims to give South Texas working people a voice outside the two major parties.

economy.evidence: General statement: his issues page says wages lag living costs and that billionaires and corporations hoard wealth, calling for systemic change.

liberty.evidence: His campaign biography says he has organized for marriage equality and reproductive rights (LGBTQ rights, abortion); no statements on guns, drugs or speech were found.

security.evidence: General statement: calls for a return to pre-9/11 normalcy and an end to terrorism fearmongering that he says has harmed communities.

immigration.evidence: His campaign site calls for abolishing ICE and says ICE, DHS and CBP operations tear immigrant families apart.

foreign.evidence: Campaigns under a Free Palestine and anti-AIPAC message, opposing current U.S. support for Israel.

energy.evidence: General statement: says climate change is a real, present problem and criticizes both parties' inaction and fossil fuel industry profits.

notes: Read the campaign home, About and On the Issues pages and the Texas Green Party candidate page; web search was unavailable, so no news questionnaires were found. No statements on healthcare, technology, schools or religion in public life were found.

name: Greg Stoker
bio: Greg Stoker is a former U.S. Army Ranger with four combat deployments to Afghanistan who was raised in South Austin and holds a Columbia University degree in anthropology and international relations. He works as a political analyst and co-host of the Colonial Outcasts podcast, and was detained by Israeli forces in 2025 while leading a veteran delegation on the Global Sumud Flotilla to Gaza. He is the Green Party nominee for Texas's 31st District.

platform.point: Says every Texan deserves affordable, comprehensive health coverage and that Americans pay the most for care in the developed world.
Says war should be a last resort and opposes lawmakers holding stock in or taking money from military contractors.
Opposes the data-center boom, citing eminent domain risks to farmland and drained aquifers used for cooling.
Warns the AI bubble may burst without delivering jobs or broad economic benefits to Texans.
Wants federal money shifted from wars toward healthcare, education, infrastructure and veterans' support.
Refuses PAC donations, including from military contractors, and opposes AIPAC and special-interest influence.
Redirect public resources toward affordability for working Texans and hold officials accountable.

economy.evidence: General statement: campaigns on 'communities over corporations' and says wealthy corporations exploit Texas communities through lower property tax revenue.

welfare.evidence: General statement: his issues page says every Texan deserves affordable, comprehensive healthcare coverage, without naming a specific program.

foreign.evidence: Runs an anti-war campaign saying war should be a last resort and opposing military-contractor influence and AIPAC.

tech.evidence: General statement: opposes the Texas data-center boom as a threat to land and water and is skeptical of the AI industry's promised benefits.

notes: Read the campaign home, About and Issues pages, the Green Party and Texas Green Party pages, and San Antonio Current coverage; he says he avoids culture-war issues, and no statements on immigration, abortion, guns, policing, schools or religion were found. The campaign image URL may be a graphic rather than a plain headshot.

name: Chris Royal
bio: Chris Royal is a Harlingen resident who moved to the Rio Grande Valley in 1993 and has worked in law, the title business and teaching. He earned a law degree from the Kansas City School of Law in 1990. He ran for this seat as an independent in 2020 and 2022 and is the Libertarian nominee in 2026.

platform.point: Hold the federal government to the Constitution and Bill of Rights as originally intended.
Require the federal government to balance its budget, as Texas does, which he says would curb inflation.
Rein in federal overspending and the growing national debt.
Limit Washington to a few core duties such as defense, postal service and interstate commerce.

economy.evidence: Campaign calls for a balanced budget and a federal government confined to a few constitutional functions.

notes: Read every page of his campaign site (home and a placeholder blog page) and the Texas Libertarian Party candidate list, which has no issue text; web search was unavailable and no questionnaires or news interviews were found. Prior runs as an independent come from Wikipedia's 2026 Texas House elections page.

name: Espoir Ngabo
bio: Espoir Ngabo came to Houston as a refugee from Congo at age 5 and works as a regional IT analyst after nearly a decade in information technology roles. He describes himself as a community advocate with ties to Alief, Sharpstown and Gulfton. He is the Green Party nominee for Texas's 7th Congressional District.

platform.point: Co-sponsor Medicare for All to create single-payer universal healthcare and oppose privatizing Medicare or Medicaid.
Raise the federal minimum wage to $25 an hour, indexed to inflation and regional living costs.
Tax net worth above $50 million, tax billionaires' unrealized gains, and expand IRS enforcement on the ultra-wealthy.
End aid to Israel, vote against unconditional military aid, cut Foreign Military Financing and recognize a Palestinian state.
Oppose Texas school voucher programs, forgive student-loan debt and restore the Department of Education.
Co-sponsor the Women's Health Protection Act and support a constitutional amendment protecting bodily autonomy.
Increase federal flood-mitigation and drainage funding for Houston and expand bus transit, including a zero-fare pilot.
Overturn Citizens United, adopt ranked-choice voting and public campaign financing, ban congressional stock trading and set term limits.

economy.evidence: His platform backs a wealth tax on fortunes above $50 million, taxing billionaires' unrealized gains and a $25 federal minimum wage.

welfare.evidence: Pledges to co-sponsor the Medicare for All Act and supports universal year-round school meals and national paid parental leave.

liberty.evidence: On abortion, backs the Women's Health Protection Act and a constitutional amendment on bodily autonomy; no stances on guns, drugs, LGBTQ rights or speech were found.

foreign.evidence: Calls for ending aid to Israel, voting against unconditional military aid, cutting Foreign Military Financing and reining in the military-industrial complex.

tech.evidence: Calls for regulating data centers over water and grid use and endorses the Data Transparency Act.

education.evidence: Opposes Texas school voucher programs and calls for restoring the federal Department of Education.

notes: Found his campaign site through the Texas Green Party candidate page and read its home, About and Platform pages; no statements on immigration, policing, energy or religion were found. The campaign photo URL is the main image on his home page and may not be a close headshot.

name: Daniel Cottam
bio: Daniel Cottam is a bariatric surgeon, business owner and medical device consultant who studied at Brigham Young University and earned his medical degree from the University of Texas. He ran for the Utah House in 2022 and for Congress in Utah's 1st District in 2024, and he has also run for governor. He has previously been registered as both a Republican and a Democrat.

platform.point: Presents his medical career as the basis for fixing the health care system.
Says government's job is to protect liberties rather than abuse them.

notes: No campaign website was found; the Utah Libertarian Party page gives only general statements and links a nomination speech video whose content could not be read. Web search was unavailable, and his Facebook page requires a login.

name: Robert Moesinger
bio: Robert Moesinger is an automation engineer who lives in Ogden and is running as an independent in Utah's 2nd Congressional District. His campaign centers on moving to a multi-party democracy to reduce partisan gridlock.

platform.point: Move beyond the two-party system so more viewpoints are represented.
Adopt institutional reforms that reduce partisan gridlock.
Change election rules so that more than two parties can be viable.
Argues the two-party system fuels lobbying and career politicians, and calls for limits on entrenched interests.
Lists debt, healthcare, housing, AI, energy and immigration among problems he says multi-party government could address.

notes: Read every page of his campaign site (problem, solution, policy, about and help pages); it lists issues such as debt, energy and AI but takes no side on them, so no topics could be scored. His occupation and hometown come from his own About page.

name: Cassie Easley
bio: Cassie Easley is an evangelical Christian who has lived in rural Utah for more than 20 years and is a certified concealed-carry and home-defense firearms instructor. She studies political science, economics and agriculture at Southern Utah University. She is the Constitution Party nominee for Utah's 3rd Congressional District in 2026.

platform.point: Says Congress should act only within the powers listed in Article I, Section 8 of the Constitution.
Argues citizens have traded freedom for perceived safety and that politicians have taken powers never delegated to them.
Strongly supports the Second Amendment, calling it the protection for the rest of the Bill of Rights.

economy.evidence: General statement: says the federal government should make no laws on matters not listed in the Constitution.

liberty.evidence: General statement on guns: calls herself a strong Second Amendment supporter without naming specific gun laws; no stances on abortion, drugs, LGBTQ rights or speech were found.

notes: Found her campaign site and read all its pages; it offers only general constitutional statements and a gun-rights stance. Web search was unavailable, and no questionnaires or news coverage were found.

name: Adonis Hooslyn
bio: Adonis Hooslyn was raised in Ogden, Utah, and holds film and business degrees from Full Sail University. He worked as an office manager and project coordinator for a Los Angeles film and TV distribution company before moving back to Utah in 2021. He is running as an unaffiliated candidate for Utah's 3rd Congressional District on a working-class platform.

platform.point: Move to a Medicare for All system, treating healthcare as a right not tied to employment or wealth.
Lower housing, grocery and utility costs and provide a robust safety net for district residents.
Protect and create jobs while regulating AI development so technology serves people over corporate profits.
Raise taxes on billionaires so they pay what he calls their fair share.
End the use of taxpayer money for foreign wars and redirect it to domestic needs.
Abolish ICE and move its funding to his core affordability and healthcare policies.
Opposes censorship and mandatory online identity verification.
Calls for transparent investigations of corruption and of cryptocurrency schemes.

economy.evidence: Calls for higher taxes on billionaires and campaigns against what he calls oligarchy and billionaire wealth hoarding.

welfare.evidence: Lists a transition to Medicare for All as one of his four core policies, alongside a robust safety net.

liberty.evidence: On speech, opposes censorship and mandatory online identity verification; no stances on abortion, guns, drugs or LGBTQ rights were found.

security.evidence: Opposes mandatory online identity verification, a specific privacy stance, though he states no views on policing or surveillance.

immigration.evidence: Calls for abolishing ICE and reallocating its funds.

foreign.evidence: Calls for ending the use of taxpayer funds for foreign wars under a 'No War' priority.

tech.evidence: General statement: calls for regulating AI development to protect jobs, while also opposing mandatory online identity verification.

notes: Found his campaign site through Wikipedia's 2026 Utah House elections page and read its single-page platform; no statements on energy, schools or religion in public life were found. No social media links or headshot URL were listed on the site.
